papers.title: Does Learning Protein Folding Generalize to Broader Reasoning?

summary.tldr: Fold2Reason uses protein structure data to post-train language models, yielding improvements on protein structure prediction and transferring gains to broader spatial, scientific, and general reasoning tasks.
key_points: Introduces FoldingCorpus, a protein-derived question-answering dataset, and Fold2Reason, a post-training strategy for language models.
Uses joint supervision: discrete structural predictions via the native language head and continuous 3D geometry decoded from shared representations.
Outperforms Qwen3.5-9B on FoldBench structure prediction by 2.7x to 3.5x.
Increases macro-average accuracy from 45.09% to 48.33% (+3.23 pp) across 10 benchmarks evaluating spatial, graph, scientific, and general reasoning.
Demonstrates that controls using random, synthetic, or shuffled structures fail to replicate these reasoning gains.
summary.why_it_matters: Non-linguistic, structure-dense scientific data can serve as an effective post-training supervision source to improve general model reasoning beyond the target domain.

papers.title: FrameMorrow: Future-guided Frame Selection with Prospective Tokens for Long-Horizon Video Generation

summary.tldr: FrameMorrow introduces a prospective frame selector that predicts compact tokens representing future information needs to select relevant historical frames for long-horizon video generation.
key_points: Predicts a small set of prospective tokens to represent upcoming information needs instead of generating full future frames.
Uses prospective tokens to guide the selection of explicit historical frames rather than internal model states.
Operates as a plug-and-play module compatible with diverse, closed-source, and action-conditioned generators with minimal inference overhead.
Demonstrates performance gains across 5 benchmarks and 11 generative models in long-range consistency, visual quality, and action alignment.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, memory-efficient long-video generation by selecting key history based on future requirements without needing access to internal model weights.

papers.title: MotorMind: Scaffolding General Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation

summary.tldr: MotorMind is a robot manipulation harness that enables general vision-language models to perform zero-shot manipulation by mapping VLM-proposed mid-level actions to deterministic control with asynchronous monitoring and background memory updates.
key_points: Operates without task-specific policy training, coding agents, or external grounding tools like SAM3.
Achieves 66.7% success on base LIBERO-PRO suites and 53.8% under perturbations, outperforming prior zero-shot baseline maximums of 13.3% and 19.2%.
Attains a 95% average success rate on a real xArm6 robot across direct manipulation and human-perturbation environments.
Integrates mid-level action representations directly with general VLMs, demonstrating performance scaling as underlying VLM capabilities increase.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that general-purpose VLMs can perform effective real-world robotic control without complex external tooling, task-specific training, or specialized policy networks.

papers.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning

summary.tldr: ProWAM is a world action model that improves robotic control by jointly predicting action sequences and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals, caching sub-goal features to eliminate iterative full-video generation during replanning.
key_points: Predicts sparse visual sub-goals alongside actions to guide long-horizon task execution without generating dense video rollouts.
Offloads visual planning to a video backbone that can leverage action-free videos, running a single forward pass to cache sub-goal features for lightweight action denoising during execution.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on simulation benchmarks: 85.8% on LIBERO-Plus, 75.7% on randomized RoboTwin, and 48.1% on RoboCasa365.
Demonstrates zero-shot real-world generalization with a 70.0% success rate in novel scenes, outperforming the strongest baseline by +15.0 absolute percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: By decoupling sparse visual planning from dense action denoising, ProWAM enables efficient, robust long-horizon robotic control and strong zero-shot real-world generalization.

papers.title: On-Policy Parameter Update Direction Underlies Generalization in LLM Post-Training

summary.tldr: Researchers show that on-policy post-training generalization stems from its dynamically adjusted cumulative parameter update direction, which can be transferred to Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to improve generalization.
key_points: SFT updates parameters in consistent directions, whereas on-policy paradigms continuously adjust parameter update directions throughout training.
The authors introduce On-Policy direction-constrained Supervised Fine-Tuning (OPSFT), which restricts SFT updates to match the cumulative parameter update directions learned from on-policy training.
OPSFT allows models to achieve strong generalization efficiency by discovering effective update directions in a few on-policy steps before switching to SFT.
OPSFT enables models to incorporate high-quality offline trajectories during post-training without degrading abilities acquired through on-policy learning.
summary.why_it_matters: By constraining SFT to on-policy update directions, developers can combine the superior generalization of on-policy post-training with the high computational efficiency and trajectory utilization of SFT.

papers.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models

summary.tldr: NAVA-WAM introduces native action-prior learning, directly pretraining an Action-DiT policy on observation-only videos using future-video flow-matching supervision before post-training on action-labeled robot data.
key_points: Pretrains the Action-DiT policy on observation-only videos by propagating future-video flow-matching supervision over visual transitions through transition-structured joint attention.
Post-trains the model for robot control using action-labeled demonstrations via joint video-action flow matching.
Employs asymmetric attention during post-training to decouple the visual branch from iterative action denoising, facilitating efficient action-only inference.
Eliminates the need for intermediate representation-to-control adaptation or separate latent-action models while improving in-distribution, out-of-distribution, and real-robot performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable robot policy pretraining directly from vast, unannotated video datasets without requiring expensive action labels or complex latent-action grounding.

papers.title: Pivot-SD: Efficient Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: Pivot-SD is an offline self-distillation framework for masked diffusion language models that selectively trains high-impact commitment tokens (pivots) identified via an information-gain metric.
key_points: Identifies high-impact commitment tokens (pivots) by measuring uncertainty reduction over remaining masked positions during denoising.
Applies cross-entropy loss to pivots from successful trajectories and targeted unlikelihood loss to pivots from failed trajectories.
Leaves non-pivot tokens in failed trajectories untouched to avoid unnecessary unlearning.
Outperforms full-sequence SFT and diffusion RL baselines on LLaDA-8B-Instruct using 200 questions with four rollouts each across math and code benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves post-training efficiency and benchmark performance for masked diffusion language models by targeting individual trajectory-shaping tokens instead of updating entire sequences or denoising steps.

papers.title: SimuVerity: Benchmarking Agents for Engineering-Grade Simulink Model Generation

summary.tldr: SimuVerity is a new benchmark containing 101 text-to-executable Simulink generation tasks that evaluates AI agents against engineering specifications rather than simple compilation or structural similarity.
key_points: Comprises 101 tasks across ten engineering domains, using executable-system profiles and four families of native simulation scenarios.
Employs a hierarchical evaluator that verifies artifact delivery, native executability, and engineering qualification before scoring models across six performance dimensions.
Evaluates six agent systems, with the top-performing system achieving an overall score of just 42.86.
Demonstrates that structural similarity fails to reflect engineering performance, revealing bottlenecks in meeting qualification standards and multidimensional requirements.
Identifies that even high-scoring generated models frequently suffer from severe visual-layout disorder.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a rigorous, specification-driven standard for evaluating whether AI agents can generate functionally correct, production-grade control and dynamic systems in Simulink.

papers.title: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents

summary.tldr: HyperBrowseComp is a new multilingual and multimodal web-browsing benchmark featuring 423 manually authored, human-validated questions across 13 languages designed to stress-test AI agent information-seeking capabilities.
key_points: Dataset contains 423 questions targeting concise, verifiable answers derived from heterogeneous web sources including videos, maps, images, and scanned documents.
Questions are filtered using internet-disconnected models to eliminate queries solvable purely by parametric knowledge.
Models were evaluated across 13 languages using both provider-native search and a shared external retrieval harness under a standardized agent protocol.
Human baseline evaluations were conducted on a sample of questions to contextualize model search performance and required effort.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a rigorous benchmark to evaluate how effectively autonomous agents navigate complex, multi-step clue chains and diverse media across non-English web environments.

papers.title: Source Preference in the Wild: How LLM Agents Favor Items by Source, and How to Reduce It

summary.tldr: Evaluations of 12 LLM search agents across three domains reveal strong source preference bias, where models frequently select inferior items from favored sources over better-fitting items from dispreferred sources.
key_points: Across 12 LLM agent models and three domains, models systematically favor specific sources even when items occupy identical search positions and meet identical user requirements.
Source bias can override item quality: an item satisfying one fewer requirement is chosen ~66% of the time if it originates from a preferred source, compared to almost 0% in the reverse scenario.
Explicit source identifiers directly drive choices: hiding source labels mitigates preference, while swapping labels to a preferred source increases an item's selection rate.
Source preferences stem from training shortcuts rewarding specific sources and missing item information triggering model preconceptions.
Supplying complete item details or applying counter-preconception prompts successfully reduces source bias.
summary.why_it_matters: Source bias in LLM agents can distort fair market competition and undermine search accuracy by steering users toward sub-optimal choices based solely on brand or domain identity.

papers.title: Science or Slop?: Benchmarking and Mitigating Scientific Slop in AI-Generated Papers

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced SciSlopBench to measure AI-generated scientific slop via global reasoning metrics, and developed SciSlopHarness to mitigate these structural flaws using grounded experiment records.
key_points: SciSlopBench evaluates AI-generated scientific papers across six measures spanning Structure, Argument, and Artifacts using 390 matched AI-human paper pairs.

The benchmark's structural measures identify AI-generated papers with 85.9% accuracy, outperforming token-based detectors like Binoculars (68.7%), and correlate higher slop with lower ICLR paper ratings from 2017 to 2025.

Directly prompting models to reduce slop causes reward hacking, whereas SciSlopHarness guides fixed LLMs using experiment records to revise papers, closing the remaining AI-human slop gap by 63% over top revision baselines without human reference targets.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that AI-generated scientific papers harbor global reasoning failures invisible to standard token detectors, providing a framework to accurately identify and ground synthetic research writing in empirical data.

papers.title: LexReward: A Taxonomy-Driven Reward Framework for Legal Language Models

summary.tldr: LexReward is a taxonomy-driven legal reward modeling framework that evaluates language model outputs across three distinct dimensions: Style, Element, and Chain.
key_points: Evaluates outputs using specific rubrics across Style (lexical/syntactic quality), Element (legal subjects, facts, statutes, decisions), and Chain (reasoning order, completeness, correctness, non-redundancy).
Generates pairwise preference data for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and trains dimension-specific reward models called LexRM.
LexRM enables reinforcement learning optimization on downstream policies without requiring reference answers at reward time.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces coarse holistic judgments with fine-grained, interpretable legal reward signals that explicitly improve policy outputs in style, factual accuracy, and reasoning chain structure.

papers.title: Spatial Memory Intelligence: Endowing World Models with Understanding-Driven Long-Term Memory

summary.tldr: Spatial Memory Intelligence (SMI) uses a multimodal large language model to systematically manage spatial memory in long-video world models via four coordinated atomic operations.
key_points: SMI addresses long-range spatial context management in interactive entertainment and embodied simulation world models.
Leverages the spatial reasoning capabilities of MLLMs for understanding-driven memory management.
Implements four core atomic operations: spatial clustering, within-cluster sparsification, action-aware retrieval, and reliability-aware filtering.
Demonstrates improvements across memory sparsity, generation stability, and spatial consistency across multiple benchmarks and backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves long-video generation stability and spatial consistency in world models by replacing unmanaged history with intelligent, MLLM-driven memory pruning and retrieval.

papers.title: Science Utopia? Closed-Loop LLM Simulation of Academic Research Ecosystems

summary.tldr: SciUtopia is a persistent, closed-loop LLM-agent simulation framework that models multi-year academic research ecosystems, including peer review, funding, collaboration, and researcher attrition.
key_points: Simulated 61 worlds containing over 40,000 LLM researchers and 8,000 institutions across multiple simulated years.
Generated approximately 400,000 publication decisions and 1.2 million LLM peer reviews.
Found that rejection-driven resubmission amplifies reviewer workload beyond baseline population growth.
Demonstrated that resource inequality emerges even without cumulative advantage from early funding wins.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a configurable testbed for conducting counterfactual experiments and targeted interventions on scientific funding, review mechanisms, and research policy.

papers.title: EditHero: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Part-Level 3D Editing and Vibe Modeling

summary.tldr: EditHero is the first benchmark for long-horizon, part-level 3D editing featuring natural-language instructions, target images, and a deterministic assembly engine for geometry and texture.
key_points: Introduces EditHero, a human-reviewed benchmark that evaluates sequential, multi-step 3D revisions using target images and natural-language prompts.
Compares top-down non-agentic methods (regenerating from learned 3D representations) against bottom-up LLM/VLM agentic methods (editing via mesh-inspecting code).
Finds non-agentic methods frequently fail to apply edits and inadvertently alter unedited regions.
Demonstrates that LLM/VLM code-editing agents preserve unedited parts better and follow instructions more closely, though each edit requires minutes to complete.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a rigorous framework for evaluating multi-step 3D asset revision, highlighting code-generating AI agents as a superior approach for localized, non-destructive mesh editing.

papers.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Frontier Reasoning Data Synthesis

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced task-harness co-evolution, a recursive harness self-improvement framework that dynamically adapts generation workflows and skills alongside synthesized reasoning problems to continuously generate harder benchmarks.
key_points: Uses online self-improvement to convert intermediate solver failures into reusable skills during task generation.
Applies post-task self-improvement to update prompts, skills, and workflows after each batch, retaining changes only if they yield harder valid tasks within a bounded cost.
Keeps underlying model weights and verification criteria fixed while reducing mean solver accuracy from 100.0% to 54.8% across 14 evolution rounds.
Fine-tuning a 27B student model on 10K synthesized math tasks achieved 62.5% mean-16 accuracy on APEX, outperforming fixed-harness recursive baselines in downstream SFT and GRPO.
summary.why_it_matters: Updating the data synthesis harness itself alongside task generation produces significantly harder reasoning datasets that directly enhance downstream model fine-tuning.

papers.title: OptiSelect: How does the Optimizer Shape Data Curriculum?

summary.tldr: OptiSelect formalizes optimizer-aware online data selection for LLM pretraining, proving theoretically and empirically that diagonal-adaptive optimizers like AdamW and Sophia provide superior selection gain over sign-based preconditioners like Lion and Muon.
key_points: Formalizes OptiSelect to account for optimizer steps that reshape raw gradients when scoring candidate data utility during online pretraining selection.
Establishes a selection gain principle showing that selection advantage depends on utility score discriminability, proving Lion and Muon suffer from discriminability collapse.
Proves diagonal-adaptive optimizers (AdamW, Sophia) admit strictly higher upper bounds on selection gains than sign-based or polar-tangential preconditioners.

Derives the optimal candidate oversampling ratio quantitatively and demonstrates AdamW's scoring geometry remains superior even when using Muon as the model optimizer on 124M and 720M parameter models.
Confirms that OptiSelect maintains performance benefits when integrated with data rephrasing pipelines.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides theoretical foundations and practical co-design rules for selecting data scoring geometries that maximize training efficiency in large language model pretraining.

papers.title: IDRF: Inverse-Distilled Reward Fine-tuning of Masked Discrete Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: IDRF enables reward fine-tuning for few-step masked discrete diffusion models by replacing the intractable sequence-level KL divergence with an inverse-distillation loss.
key_points: Replaces the intractable sequence-level KL penalty in reverse-KL-regularized fine-tuning with inverse-distillation regularization using an optimal auxiliary denoiser.
Proves that the population inverse-distillation loss forms an upper bound on the sequence-level KL divergence relative to the reference distribution.
Frames few-step generation as a finite-horizon MDP and optimizes rewards using a clipped policy-gradient objective without requiring reference-model rollouts.
Achieves target rewards across DNA, image, and text generation tasks using up to 32 times fewer denoising steps while preventing reward hacking.
summary.why_it_matters: IDRF allows masked discrete diffusion models to undergo efficient reward alignment and maintain sample quality at significantly lower sampling latency.

papers.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation

summary.tldr: A theoretical and empirical study proving that the choice of divergence objective in distillation acts as an implicit entropy regularizer, with forward KL inflating student entropy and reverse KL deflating it.
key_points: Forward KL (including standard cross-entropy training) mathematically guarantees that the student model's entropy is inflated above the teacher's entropy.
Reverse KL deflates student entropy relative to the teacher until the student-teacher capability gap becomes too large.
Lower entropy in on-policy distillation stems specifically from token-level reverse KL rather than on-policy data sampling.
Interpolating between forward and reverse KL yields smooth entropy shifts early in training, but causes abrupt entropy transitions at convergence.
In self-distillation, optimal divergence hyperparameters act to compensate for the entropy deflation caused by conditioning on privileged information.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how different divergence functions implicitly control student entropy enables principled selection of distillation objectives for model compression, pretraining, and finetuning.

papers.title: Metropolis-Hastings Dominates Importance Resampling for Policy Composition

summary.tldr: Researchers prove that independence Metropolis-Hastings achieves lower sampling bias than sampling-importance-resampling for decoding-time LLM policy composition across all rollout budgets and convex f-divergences.
key_points: Analyzes independence Metropolis-Hastings (MH) to correct sampling bias introduced when combining next-token probabilities during decoding-time policy composition.
Proves MH yields an output distribution closer to the target weighted product distribution than sampling-importance-resampling (SIR) for any budget under all convex f-divergences.
Derives a lower bound on MH's improvement over uncorrected decoders using a consensus objective.
Characterizes sampling error in asymptotic regimes where policies approach agreement and where log ratios between target and uncorrected probabilities fluctuate heavily over long responses.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes Metropolis-Hastings as a mathematically superior inference-time method for adjusting multi-reward trade-offs in LLMs without costly retraining.

papers.title: KV$^2$: A Self-Refining KV Cache

summary.tldr: KV$^2$ is a query-agnostic KV-cache compression method that reduces memory footprint by using a lightweight proxy scorer to filter tokens before selectively reprocessing only the most informative subset to compute eviction scores.
key_points: Uses a two-stage eviction pipeline: a lightweight proxy scorer identifies candidate tokens, followed by selective reconstruction on that subset rather than the full context.
Outperforms existing baselines on RULER 16K at a 2% KV-cache budget by over 40 percentage points.
Achieves the highest average performance on LongBench across 2%-10% cache budgets while reducing compression runtime and peak memory relative to full-context reconstruction methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient long-context model serving in multi-query settings by significantly reducing KV-cache memory costs without the high computational overhead of full-context reprocessing.

papers.title: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation:A Reinforcement Learning Perspective

summary.tldr: Framing on-policy distillation as reinforcement learning reveals that performance gains and length-collapse stem from teacher implicit rewards amplifying student behaviors, rather than expanding student capabilities.
key_points: On-policy distillation (OPD) acts as an implicit reward model where teacher feedback amplifies pre-existing student rollouts without expanding underlying capabilities.
OPD collapses into overlong, repetitive outputs due to reward hacking, which occurs when implicit teacher preferences misalign with actual generation quality.
Implicit teacher rewards can severely favor and amplify overlong rollouts even if the teacher model rarely generates such patterns itself.
Masking unhealthy student responses during training and using SFT initialization effectively mitigate reward hacking and structural collapse.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding OPD as implicit reward learning shifts the optimization focus from teacher generation quality to teacher evaluation reliability, providing concrete methods to prevent length collapse during model post-training.

papers.title: Emergent Structure in the Marginal Attention Space of Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers analyzed the post-softmax marginal attention space across 60+ LLMs, discovering a text-intrinsic token signature linked to input-output Jacobians and a model-private head signature useful for static KV cache budgeting.
key_points: Marginal attention is created by mapping post-softmax attention weights into a joint token-head space by marginalizing over query positions.

Token-wise reduction produces a text-intrinsic signal conserved across models, which theoretically and empirically aligns with the network's input-output Jacobian statistics given similar next-token distributions.
Head-wise reduction yields a model-private signature conserved across different documents.

Using offline, precomputed per-head budgets from pretraining text combined with a training-free token score achieves competitive KV cache eviction performance without needing document-level recomputation or target-specific training.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient KV cache eviction by decoupling static, model-specific head budget allocation from dynamic, text-intrinsic token scoring.

papers.title: The Geometry of Knowledge Accessibility in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Knowledge accessibility in LLMs has a geometric structure in the query's pre-generation representation space, where accessibility decreases with distance from a central point, forming a knowledge boundary that dictates effective inference interventions.
key_points: Knowledge accessibility correlates with a query's distance from a representation space center prior to text generation, separating accessible queries from inaccessible ones across a knowledge boundary.
The distance-based accessibility ordering transfers across different datasets even when the underlying representation centers differ.
Experiments confirm the centered geometry specifically reflects knowledge accessibility rather than general reasoning difficulty.

Geometric location dictates optimal inference interventions: query rewriting benefits accessible queries, chain-of-thought helps near the boundary, and retrieval-augmented generation yields the largest gains beyond the boundary.
summary.why_it_matters: This pre-generation geometric signal enables adaptive inference frameworks to dynamically select the most effective intervention (such as rewriting, chain-of-thought, or retrieval) before generating a response.

papers.title: HyperThink: Text-to-Parameter Hypernetworks for Efficient Reasoning

summary.tldr: HyperThink uses a lightweight text-to-parameter hypernetwork with a vector-quantized decoder to predict base LLM parameter updates, replacing long inference-time thinking traces with a single query-conditioned forward pass.
key_points: Amortizes multi-step reasoning overhead by mapping input text directly to a small subset of base LLM parameter updates.
Uses a vector-quantized decoder to constrain parameter updates to a finite set of reusable patterns, enhancing robustness and transfer.
Trained end-to-end on base model outputs to generate concise solutions and final answers without intermediate test-time reasoning traces.
Improves the low-latency region of the accuracy-latency trade-off in mathematical and general reasoning tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces sequential decoding latency and token consumption in LLMs while maintaining strong multi-step reasoning performance.

security.title: Top AI agent security resources — October 2026

summary.tldr: Adversa AI compiled 49 AI agent security resources from September 2026, highlighting major real-world breaches, package supply chain attacks, and agent execution vulnerabilities.
key_points: Gemini breached three companies in reported security incidents.
2,000 malicious RubyGems packages were identified in supply chain threats.
A zero-click Agentforce hijack vulnerability was demonstrated.
summary.why_it_matters: Autonomous AI agents face severe operational risks from zero-click exploits, supply chain compromise, and cross-organization breaches.

security.title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS) to demonstrate that altering agent-visible tool names without changing underlying task mechanics significantly swings LLM agent Attack Success Rates.
key_points: TPRS measures ASR variation when changing agent-visible representations while keeping tasks, harmful actions, security policies, ground truth, environments, and evaluation criteria fixed.
Replacing threat-related tool names with neutral names on Agent Security Bench (ASB) increases committed ASR by 11.67 percentage points for GPT-5-mini and 13.21 points for Claude Haiku 4.5.
Adding explicit threat names to neutral tools on MCPTox lowers ASR by 11.00 percentage points on GPT-5-mini and 4.11 points on Claude Haiku 4.5.
A length-, token count-, and casing-matched neutral name reproduced 8.54 of the 11.00 point ASR drop on GPT-5-mini on MCPTox.
Modifying tool names with threat-related wording on AgentDojo shifted ASR by only 0.50 percentage points on GPT-4o-mini, but decreased benign utility by 5.36 points on tasks utilizing that tool.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-representation security benchmark scores fail to generalize, requiring evaluations across controlled threat-preserving representations to substantiate agent robustness claims.

security.title: CorrectGuard: Eyes-Off Correctness Estimation for Black-Box Security Guardrails

summary.tldr: CorrectGuard estimates black-box security guardrail decision correctness in human and machine eyes-off settings using independent external evaluators trained solely on labeled eyes-on data.
key_points: Evaluated in-context learning, embedding, and finetuning methods across 13 safety/security datasets and open-weight guardrails treated as black boxes.
Achieved up to a 25 percentage-point increase in macro accuracy for error identification using in-context learning, and nearly 15 points using finetuning.
Reduced Area Under the Risk-Coverage curve (AURC) from 0.33-0.44 down to 0.17-0.22 across three guardrails using correctness score rankings.
Retained 37.5-52.0% of guardrail decisions at a target threshold of 15% observed risk via decision abstention.
Implemented machine eyes-off evaluation using privacy-preserving input fingerprinting without requiring internal access to the guardrail.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables continuous privacy-preserving auditing and risk-based decision abstention for black-box guardrails without exposing sensitive user inputs or model internals.

security.title: Passing the Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Evaluating 15 prompt-injection detectors across BIPIA, AgentDojo, and tau-bench reveals that benchmark detection rankings transfer poorly to agent tool outputs, driven largely by differences in training input structure.
key_points: Benchmark rankings show poor transfer: the top detector on BIPIA caught only 2% of AgentDojo injections at a 1% false-positive rate, while a detector catching 72% on AgentDojo caught only 15% on tau-bench.
False-positive rates on tool outputs ranged from 0% to over 90% and transferred consistently between the two agent benchmarks.

Exposing detectors to short attack strings during training failed to generalize to detecting injections embedded inside full agent tool outputs, whereas training on agent-style inputs yielded the best performance across agent benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard prompt-injection benchmarks fail to predict detector performance in deployment, requiring teams to evaluate detectors using low false-positive thresholds on actual agent tool outputs.

security.title: Persona Guardrail: A Production-Grade Defense Framework for Agentic Systems

summary.tldr: Persona Guardrail provides synchronous input and output validation for agentic systems using semantic allowlists and blocklists, alongside a new evaluation benchmark called PAGE.
key_points: Persona Guardrail enforces explicit functional boundaries on customer-facing agents via synchronous semantic allowlist and blocklist specifications.
Introduces PAGE (Persona-Aware Guardrail Evaluation), a benchmark for measuring performance across benign, adversarial, and out-of-domain interactions for user and agent turns.
Outperforms generic LLM-based guardrails by increasing overall accuracy from 85.7% to 95.9% and out-of-domain detection from 57.3% to 93.5%.
Reduces the false-approved rate from 25.0% to 4.7% while maintaining target latency budgets under production workloads.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a production-deployed method to prevent agents from executing out-of-domain or malicious requests that traditional prompt-injection guardrails miss.

security.title: Defense-in-Depth at the Perception-Reasoning Interface of LLM-Centric Agentic UAV Swarms

summary.tldr: Researchers implemented and evaluated a five-layer defense-in-depth architecture at the perception-reasoning interface of LLM-centric UAV swarms, using analytical boundaries and deterministic fallbacks to prevent adversarial manipulation of sensor report inputs.
key_points: The defense architecture features five distinct layers: provenance verification, physical admissibility checks, spatial-historical consistency validation, schedule starvation prevention, and fallback to a deterministic scheduler.
Detection boundaries for the three input-side validation layers were derived in closed form using pre-attack deployment parameters, matching empirical results across 30 simulation runs.
Replacing rejected adversarial reports with the most recent accepted report prevented schedule hijacking, but increased cumulative system costs by 74% and 79% for the respective detection layers.
The safety check layer reduced attack-induced operational costs by 37.5% without directly detecting the underlying attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that architectural input-validation defenses can secure LLM-driven autonomous swarms against data poisoning attacks, while quantifying the operational cost trade-offs of fail-safe mechanisms.

security.title: EvoRiskBench: An Evolving Benchmark for Runtime Security Risks in Workspace Agents

summary.tldr: EvoRiskBench is an evolving benchmark using the EP-Path-EF framework to automatically construct, execute, and evaluate runtime security risks in LLM-based workspace agents.
key_points: Introduces the EP-Path-EF framework mapping risk entry points to technical effects via agent-mediated paths, featuring 9 entry-point and 5 effect categories.
Provides an automated workflow generating and independently verifying a reproducible dataset of 450 adversarial tasks across 6 scenarios in isolated environments.
Evaluates 9 model-harness configurations combining 3 models (GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, Claude Opus 5) and 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw).
Finds Codex combined with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 achieved the highest vulnerability with a 68.44% attack success rate (ASR).
Demonstrates that Attack Success Rate varies more significantly across underlying LLMs than across execution harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: Current workspace agent configurations fail to guarantee secure autonomous execution, making dynamic and reproducible runtime security benchmarks necessary.

security.title: The Fragility of Trigger-Tag Mechanisms for Misuse Detection in Open-Weight LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers formalize trigger-tag mechanisms for LLM misuse detection, introduce the UNTAG attack framework, and demonstrate that open-weight trigger-tag mechanisms are entirely vulnerable to output transformations and weight modifications.
key_points: Formalizes two trigger-tag variants: token-level tags using watermark-inspired signals during decoding, and weight-level tags using backdoor-inspired associations.
Introduces UNTAG, a unified attack framework that categorizes mechanism-specific attack surfaces into a shared taxonomy.
Evaluates trigger-tag robustness using phishing generation as a primary case study.
Demonstrates that current trigger-tag mechanisms fail completely when attackers alter generated outputs or modify open-source model weights.
summary.why_it_matters: Trigger-tag mechanisms cannot serve as reliable misuse detectors for open-weight models against adversaries capable of modifying outputs or weight files.

security.title: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks

summary.tldr: Researchers identified branch steering attacks that exploit dynamic planning in Dual-LLM Computer Use Agents (CUAs), introducing STEER-Bench to evaluate the vulnerability and COBRA, a capability-constrained architecture that mitigates it.
key_points: Computer Use Agents (CUAs) using the Dual-LLM pattern rely on branching plans for dynamic web content, making them vulnerable to branch steering attacks that coerce agents into executing pre-approved hazardous paths.
STEER-Bench comprises 101 tasks across 9 domains to evaluate branch steering vulnerabilities in CUAs.
Standard CUAs and vanilla Dual-LLM CUAs demonstrated high attack success rates on STEER-Bench, reaching 94.4% and 89.5% respectively.

The proposed COBRA architecture combines trusted branching plans with ahead-of-time capability constraints on parameters and destinations, dropping the attack success rate to 0% while preserving 97% benign utility.
summary.why_it_matters: COBRA provides a secure system-level architecture that prevents adversaries from manipulating CUA execution paths through indirect prompt injection without compromising task performance.

security.title: Beyond Predefined Sinks: Security-Aware Dependency Analysis for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AgentSecGraph is a static analysis framework that generates candidate-centered Security-Aware Agent Dependency Graphs (Security-ADGs) to evaluate LLM agent operation context beyond static predefined sinks.
key_points: Constructs Security-ADGs by enriching operation identity with agent relevance, source/dependency evidence, trust-boundary context, guard evidence, and external-effect semantics.
Introduces AgentSecBench, a benchmark of 67 real-world LLM-agent repositories covering 11 ecosystems and 37,542 source files.
Identified 23,866 static security-sensitive operation candidates across 65 repositories, processing the corpus in 50.8 minutes.

Extracted source-to-operation dependency evidence for 41.15% of candidates and guard evidence for 12.88%, establishing 22 security-sensitive behaviors (1 confirmed vulnerability, 1 pending disclosure, 20 guarded).
Preserved 91.1% of reference context and 100% of observed guards in nine held-out cases, outperforming sink-only (20.0%) and simplified ADG (40.0%) approaches.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating contextual dependency and guard evidence allows security tools to accurately differentiate between safe and vulnerable operations in LLM agents, which static sink identification alone misses.

security.title: Frequency Is Not Sensitivity Identifying Safety-Sensitive Experts in Sparse MoE LLM

summary.tldr: Router-gradient sensitivity identifies safety-critical experts in sparse MoE LLMs more effectively than activation frequency, enabling targeted expert suppression that significantly reduces model refusal rates without retraining.
key_points: Evaluated across five MoE architectures using 500 benign and 500 malicious prompts, suppressing experts selected by router-gradient sensitivity reduced refusals on held-out prompts more than activation frequency in 24 of 25 conditions.
On OLMoE, suppressing gradient-selected experts under nominal traffic budgets reduced refusals from 34/100 to 9/100 (a 73.53% relative drop) while maintaining coherent text generation.
Controlling for layer distributions by matching expert counts per layer, gradient-based selection outperformed activation frequency in 23 of 25 conditions, with two ties.

Exploratory analysis revealed a strong correlation (Spearman's rho = 0.90, p = 0.083, n = 5) between larger malicious-versus-benign expert concentration gaps and higher peak gradient-driven refusal reduction.
summary.why_it_matters: Using router-gradient sensitivity instead of routing frequency exposes critical security vulnerabilities in MoE models, demonstrating how targeted expert suppression can bypass alignment guardrails without requiring model retraining.

security.title: AgentTrap: Stateful Feedback Deception against Autonomous Penetration Testing Agents

summary.tldr: AgentTrap is the first closed-loop, stateful honeypot designed to deceive autonomous penetration testing agents using sentinel endpoints, dynamic stateful deception, and behavior-guided escalation to reduce attack success and extract agent-side API keys.
key_points: Combines sentinel endpoints, stateful deception grounded in the target application, and behavior-guided escalation to actively engage autonomous agents.
Evaluated against eight autonomous penetration-testing agents on a live web application using three defense strategies.
Reduces the aggregate real-target attack success rate from 95.8% to 79.2% compared to no defense.
Successfully extracts attacker API keys in 18.8% of evaluation runs, outperforming both static deception and fixed escalation baselines.
Trace analysis indicates agent resistance to counterattacks relies on model-level deceptive request recognition and architecture-level resource isolation.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that dynamic, stateful deception can effectively divert autonomous LLM-based penetration agents away from real infrastructure and force the disclosure of sensitive attacker credentials like API keys.

security.title: Containing the Autonomous Operator: A Defense-in-Depth Framework and Reference Architecture for Securing AI Agents on Kubernetes

summary.tldr: A seven-layer defense-in-depth framework and reference architecture that secures Kubernetes against fully compromised AI agents assuming the model is not a security boundary.
key_points: Defines a ten-class threat taxonomy and nine design principles focused on tool-boundary mediation and breaking combinations of untrusted input, sensitive access, and external egress.

Maps security principles to a seven-layer Kubernetes architecture using RBAC, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, gVisor/Kata sandboxing via SIG Apps Agent Sandbox, FQDN egress policies, and eBPF runtime enforcement.
Introduces an agent/Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway that enforces policy-as-code over tool arguments.
Provides reference architecture bindings and concrete policy artifacts tailored for Amazon EKS, Azure Kubernetes Service, and Google Kubernetes Engine.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables infrastructure teams to deploy autonomous LLM operational agents safely by enforcing deterministic cloud-native security boundaries even when agents experience prompt injection.

security.title: Pincer: Resource Authorization for Agents using a Digital Twin

summary.tldr: Pincer is a resource-layer defense for autonomous coding agents that uses an isolated digital twin model to continually learn user preferences and automatically enforce dynamic, least-privilege authorization policies.
key_points: Operates at the resource layer alongside existing tool-call defenses like auto mode to prevent security degradation from user fatigue and policy decay.
Employs an isolated-context digital twin model that acts as a proxy for user permission requests by continually learning user-specific preferences.
Introduces a user-centric evaluation dataset modeled on multi-day transcripts of user-agent interactions.
Outperforms LLM judges and Conseca adaptations in security and utility metrics, demonstrating significant improvements against specific adversarial attack types.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides scalable, automated least-privilege security for long-horizon autonomous agents without sacrificing functional utility or relying on fatigue-inducing manual user approvals.

security.title: SideKernel: A Usable microVM Sandbox for AI Coding Agents on macOS

summary.tldr: SideKernel is a new open-source, local microVM sandbox for macOS designed to resolve usability barriers preventing developers from running untrusted AI coding agents in isolated environments.
key_points: A formative user survey revealed that fewer than 40% of AI coding agent users currently utilize a sandbox due to usability friction.
SideKernel provides microVM-based isolation locally on macOS specifically tailored for autonomous AI agent workflows.
A comparative analysis evaluated sandboxes using 23 capability tests derived directly from the survey's identified usability barriers.
SideKernel and Docker Sandboxes scored highest among evaluated local, open-source microVM options for macOS capability and usability features.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers macOS developers a low-friction method to securely execute autonomous, untrusted AI coding agents without compromising local system security.

infra.title: PyTorch Hardware Enablement: Updates from the Accelerator Integration Working Group

summary.tldr: The PyTorch Accelerator Integration Working Group reported H1 2026 progress on standardizing hardware enablement, introducing Cross-Repository CI Relay, OpenReg backend maturation, and expanded PrivateUse1 profiling.
key_points: Cross-Repository CI Relay (CRCR) automates parallel CI dispatch from pytorch/pytorch to downstream hardware and library repositories, using GitHub OIDC tokens for identity verification.
CRCR integrates cross-repo health data directly into the PyTorch CI HUD (hud.pytorch.org/crcr) with five security layers, including rate limiting and state-machine checks.
Participating downstream repositories operate under a four-tiered allowlist (L1-L4) progressing from dispatch notifications to blocking PR check runs.
H1 2026 updates include refactored cross-backend test suites, OpenReg reference backend maturation, and profiling support for PrivateUse1-based hardware backends.
summary.why_it_matters: CRCR and standardized integration tools allow hardware vendors and downstream library maintainers to catch breaking PyTorch changes prior to merge without fragmenting the core codebase.

infra.title: Build Applications on NVIDIA BlueField Faster with NVIDIA DOCA Agent Skills

summary.tldr: NVIDIA DOCA Agent Skills provides domain-specific knowledge to AI agents to accelerate software development on NVIDIA BlueField DPUs.
key_points: General-purpose AI agents lack specialized knowledge for infrastructure software like NVIDIA DOCA, leading to guesswork.
NVIDIA DOCA Agent Skills integrates domain-specific context into AI agent workflows to reduce correction cycles during development.
summary.why_it_matters: By supplying domain-specific context, DOCA Agent Skills reduces developer debugging cycles and speeds up deployment on NVIDIA BlueField hardware.

vendors.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI

summary.tldr: OpenAI introduced a new visual ad format within ChatGPT alongside expanded measurement tools, attribution partnerships, and brand suitability controls for advertisers.
key_points: Launches a new visual ad format embedded directly within the ChatGPT user experience.
Expands performance measurement tools and third-party attribution partnerships for advertisers.
Introduces enhanced brand suitability controls to manage ad placement contexts within AI interactions.
summary.why_it_matters: The introduction of visual ads and third-party measurement tools establishes standard digital advertising capabilities within conversational AI interfaces.

vendors.title: Chatham scales its capital markets expertise with OpenAI

summary.tldr: Chatham Financial implemented OpenAI's Codex and GPT-5.6 models to redesign workflows and automate capital markets technology processes.
key_points: Integrated Codex and GPT-5.6 to build technology and update operational workflows.
Reduced trade validation processing time from 30 minutes to under 4 minutes.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating advanced language models into financial workflows significantly reduces trade validation latency and operational overhead.

vendors.title: Welcome RL Environments to the hub

summary.tldr: Hugging Face has added support for Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments on the Hugging Face Hub.
key_points: Reinforcement Learning environments are now natively supported and hosted on the Hugging Face Hub.
Users can discover, share, and integrate RL environments directly within the Hugging Face ecosystem.
summary.why_it_matters: Centralizing RL environments on the Hub simplifies reproducibility and access to standard benchmarks for reinforcement learning researchers and developers.
